newsitem.title: NORWAY: Operators plan to cut output at Statfjord, Snorre.
newsitem.headline: Operators plan to cut output at Statfjord, Snorre.

text.p: Oil production at the North Sea Statfjord and Snorre developments will be reduced or shut in later on Tuesday because of brimming storage capacity as bad weather delays oil loadings, the operators said.

Output at the Statfjord A and B platforms is due to be reduced to 90 percent at 1700 GMT, while throughput will be cut by 10 percent at the Statfjord C platform at 0700 GMT on Wednesday, Den norske stats oljeselskap AS said.

Statfjord pumps about 380,000 barrels per day (bpd) and processes oil from the Statfjord East and North satellites and the nearby Snorre development, which add roughly 370,000 bpd to the Statfjord stream.
Gullfaks produces around 475,000 bpd and handles around 115,000 bpd from the Tordis and Vigdis fields.
Operator of Snorre, Tordis and Vigdis, Saga Petroleum ASA, said Snorre would shut down completely "at some time during the night".
Operations at Vigdis and Tordis would continue normally for the next three to four days as long as there was storage capacity at Gullfaks, Saga said.
